cards.explanation: The answer is False, friends. The text says Zedekiah, his officers and the people of the land "…refused to obey the words that the LORD had spoken through Jeremiah the prophet." (Jeremiah 37:2) The words came through Jeremiah, and the king, his officers and the people of the land refused to obey them. That's like hearing the oven timer and deciding it's a suggestion.

The message is "Please pray to the LORD our God for us!" (Jeremiah 37:3) Jehucal and Zephaniah carry it from King Zedekiah to Jeremiah. The king asks for prayer and still hasn't obeyed. I'd call that a strange order of things, and I'd also say the text just reports it and leaves it there.

The answer is "withdraw from," friends. The Chaldeans, who were besieging Jerusalem, heard the report and "…withdrew from Jerusalem." (Jeremiah 37:5) The army that had been besieging the city pulled back. I bet that gave the city a little room to breathe.

The answer is that Pharaoh's army goes back to its own land of Egypt, friends. The LORD says that army, "…which has marched out to help you, will go back to its own land of Egypt." (Jeremiah 37:7) The army that marched out to help is going to go home. So Judah can't build its hopes on it.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says that after Pharaoh's army goes back, "…the Chaldeans will return and fight against this city. They will capture it and burn it down." (Jeremiah 37:8) It's a hard word to hear. The city's break from the siege won't last.

The answer is that they would get up and burn the city down, friends. The LORD says that even if only wounded men remained in their tents, "…they would still get up and burn this city down." (Jeremiah 37:10) Wounded men still getting up to finish the job! That tells you how sure this word is.

The answer is to claim his portion there among the people, friends. Jeremiah started to leave Jerusalem "…to go to the land of Benjamin to claim his portion there among the people." (Jeremiah 37:12) That's the reason the text gives. It's a plain errand, and it's about to go sideways.

The answer is Chaldeans, friends. Irijah seized Jeremiah and said, "You are deserting to the Chaldeans!" (Jeremiah 37:13) The Chaldeans were the army that had been besieging the city. So it was a serious thing to say about a man at the gate.

The answer is the officials, friends. Jeremiah said it was a lie, but Irijah "…would not listen to him; instead, he arrested Jeremiah and took him to the officials." (Jeremiah 37:14) No listening at all. I think that must have stung.

The answer is angry, friends. "The officials were angry with Jeremiah…" (Jeremiah 37:15) The text gives that feeling plainly. The very next thing it says is that they beat him and placed him in jail. I think this part of the story is a heavy one.

The word is that Zedekiah will be handed to Babylon's king, friends. Jeremiah answers the king, "You will be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon." (Jeremiah 37:17) After all that time in the dungeon, he still gives the word straight. I think that took real courage.

The answer is True, friends. Jeremiah asks, "How have I sinned against you or your servants or these people, that you have put me in prison?" (Jeremiah 37:18) He asks the king straight to his face. I think that's a man who knows he did nothing to earn this.

The answer is that Babylon's king would not come against them, friends. Jeremiah asks, "Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, claiming, ‘The king of Babylon will not come against you or this land’?" (Jeremiah 37:19) Those prophets claimed Babylon's king would not come against them, and Jeremiah asks where they are now. That's a hard question to answer.

The answer is False, friends. After Jeremiah's plea, "…King Zedekiah gave orders for Jeremiah to be placed in the courtyard of the guard…" (Jeremiah 37:21) The king didn't send him back to Jonathan's house. Jeremiah's petition was heard.

The answer is bakers, friends! Jeremiah got "…a loaf of bread daily from the street of the bakers…" (Jeremiah 37:21) That's a street I'd like to visit. The bread kept coming until all the bread in the city was gone.
